page.layout: One column of running text, set in full width. Below the last line, at the right, the catchword "Eph.". Page number at the top left. Running head at the top centre. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: homicidii,furti &c. tantum abesse oportere ab
eo, ut nos qui Christo nomen nostrum dedi-
mus, moveamur iis inspectis ad peccandum si-
militer, ut contra iis ipsis moveamur ad detesta-
tionem & fugam peccati. Et revera quotquot
veri[?] illuminati sunt a facie Christi,quę se viden-
dam offert in gloriosò isto Evangelio; quanto
magis in aliis vident opera illa tenebrarum, tanto
magis ab ipsis abhorrent,eaq; detestantur. Ute-
nim in hoc Evangelii speculo intuentur glori-
am Christi; ita ex adverso, in eodem hoc speculo
intuentur fœditatem atq; ignominiam illorum
operum & peccatorum: Intuiti autem eorum fœ-
ditatem, ab iis ipsis abhorrent. abhorrent, in-
quam, ab idololatria, abhorrent a blasphemia in
Deum, ab homicidio, a furto, ab adulterio, & cæ-
teris ejus farinæ. Unde est quòd ego perfuadeam
mihi, istos qui inspecto idololatrico cultu, sic
fascinatur, ut a veritate descifcant, istos, inquâ,
luce Evangelii, & facie Jesu Christi nunquam
verè ac solidè illuminatos fuisse. Quòd si enim
fuissent; profectò nequaquam passi fuissent se
tam citò, deserta veritate, transferri ad menda-
cia. Observa deinde ex hoc loco, quodnam fue-
rit peccatū, cui maximè gentes erant obnoxiæ,
& quod inter eas maximè regnabat: fuit autem
(ut licet ex hoc loco, & ex aliis pluribus, ut Rom.
1.24. & deinceps, Eph.4.19. colligere) fuit, in-
quam, peccatum hoc libidinis. Causam autem
hujus peccati inter gentes regnantis notat hoc
loco Apostolus, ignorantiam Dei, Rom.1.28.&

page.notes: The word "veri" in the line "veri illuminati" is printed with a mark that is hard to read; the reading is doubtful. "Quòd" and "quòd" keep the printed grave accent. Long s was rendered as plain s throughout (e.g. "abesse", "fuisse", "Christo", "Causam"). A stray dot and a mark in the left and right margins are printer's marks or show-through, not text. The page number is printed in old-style figures ("I2o") and is given here as 120. The text ends mid-sentence at the line "&", and "Eph." below it is the catchword. The Greek mark "‑" in the right margin is a printer's mark.
